title: Detect awaiting-reply from the Sent folder instead of inferring it
description:
Today `awaiting-reply` is one of the twelve labels in `VALID_LABELS`
(foxhole.js:10) and Claude assigns it from the prompt's description at
foxhole.js:93: "You sent or need to send a response and are waiting to hear
back." That is a judgment call made from 500 characters of a single inbound
message, so the classifier cannot actually know whether you replied.

Replace the guess with a fact. Query the Sent folder, cross-reference thread ids
against inbox threads, and apply `awaiting-reply` when you sent the last message
in a thread and no reply has arrived since.
design:
Open question the implementation must settle: whether `awaiting-reply` stays in
`VALID_LABELS` and the prompt (foxhole.js:10, :93) as a Claude-assignable label,
or is removed from both so only the deterministic check can apply it. Removing it
is cleaner, but it changes the idempotency contract, because presence of any
`VALID_LABELS` label is what marks a thread processed (see the Idempotency
section of CLAUDE.md).

Cost: this adds Gmail reads per run, on top of the current inbox search. The TODO
called that out as "additional API quota but a high-value label."
acceptance_criteria:
- A thread whose last message is from the account owner, with no later inbound reply, receives the `awaiting-reply` label.
- A thread whose last message is inbound does not receive `awaiting-reply`.
- The Sent-folder check runs without Claude deciding `awaiting-reply`, so the label no longer depends on the classifier's guess.
- A run over an inbox with no sent threads applies no `awaiting-reply` labels and raises no error.
- The added Gmail reads stay inside the Apps Script quota for a 2-minute trigger.
notes: Converted from TODO.md item 1. The original text said to apply `_auto/awaiting-reply`; that prefix is stale, since LABEL_PREFIX is '' (foxhole.js:8) and labels are top-level.

title: Install the tadw bead-label hook for Claude Code and Codex (tadw 5.0.2)
description:
**Ask:** Bring the tadw bead-label hook scripts for Claude Code and Codex current with templeton-agentic-dev-workbench 5.0.2, and wire the Codex runner in .codex/hooks.json where this repository has Codex hooks.

## Why (Computational)

install_label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh --agent both --check on 2026-10-29 reported 0 drifted and 15 not installed hook files. Without the report validators and the Stop module, pending labels (implemented, qa-d, accepted) never resolve. The installer does not edit .codex/hooks.json, and the Codex runner does nothing until that file names it.

## Estimated size

N/A (operational): copied hook scripts and one hooks.json change, no code written by hand.
acceptance_criteria: install_label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh --agent both --check exits 0 from the repo root. Where .codex/hooks.json exists, UserPromptSubmit and Stop route through .codex/scripts/run_codex_bead_hooks.sh.

title: Judge a thread on the whole conversation, not just its latest message
description:
CONTEXT.md defines a Thread as "judged as a whole: every message in it is
evidence, not just the newest one." The code does not do that. `classifyNewEmails()`
takes `messages[messages.length - 1]` (foxhole.js:44) and sends that one message
to Claude, then labels the entire thread from it.

Close the gap: send Claude the conversation rather than its last message.
design:
This matters less often than it sounds. Most threads arrive as one unread message
and are classified on the spot, where whole-conversation and latest-message are
the same thing. The two differ only for a thread that already has history when
Foxhole first sees it: a forwarded chain, a thread you were copied into late, or
a backlog built up while the trigger was failing.

Decide what "the whole conversation" is worth in tokens. Options, cheapest first:
all subjects plus the newest body; the first and newest bodies; every body
truncated to a smaller per-message budget. `max_tokens` is 64 on the response and
does not need to change; this is input size only.

Sender and From are taken from the newest message today. Keep that, because the
Sender Cache is keyed on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A thread that already holds several messages when Foxhole first sees it is classified from all of them, not only the newest.
- A thread holding one message produces the same verdict it does today.
- The evidence sent to Claude stays within a stated size ceiling, so a 200-message thread cannot blow up one request.
- `MAX_BODY_LENGTH` is redefined or replaced deliberately, since 500 characters per thread and 500 per message are different budgets.
- Per ADR 0001, this changes only what the single verdict is judged on. It does not re-judge an already labeled thread.
notes: Raised by the domain-modeling session that wrote CONTEXT.md. The glossary records the intended model; this bead makes the code match it.

title: Add a 1-5 priority score as nested Gmail labels
description:
The twelve labels in `VALID_LABELS` (foxhole.js:10) are flat and categorical, so
`urgent` is the only signal of how much something matters, and it is binary.

Add a graded score of 1 to 5 alongside the category label. Gmail has no native
priority field, so express the score as nested labels: `priority/1-critical`,
`priority/3-normal`, and so on. Nesting makes Gmail render them as one collapsible
group rather than five unrelated labels.
design:
Two decisions the implementation must make.

First, the idempotency contract. A thread counts as processed when it carries any
`VALID_LABELS` label (see CLAUDE.md). Priority labels must either join
`VALID_LABELS` and the exclusion query built at foxhole.js:32, or be excluded
from it deliberately. Getting this wrong either re-processes every thread forever
or stops processing threads that have a priority but no category.

Second, `max_tokens` is 64 (CLAUDE.md), sized for a short JSON array. Returning a
score as well as the labels needs a response shape change and probably a higher
cap. Measure before raising it.

Relationship to `urgent`: a score of 1 and the `urgent` label overlap. Decide
whether `urgent` survives as a category, or is replaced by the score.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every classified thread receives exactly one `priority/<n>-<name>` label, with n from 1 to 5.
- The five priority labels exist with distinct colors, created the same way as the current labels in `ensureLabelsExist()`.
- Claude returns the score in the same response as the category labels, so the run still makes one API call per batch.
- A score outside 1 to 5, or a missing score, falls back to `priority/3-normal` rather than leaving the thread unscored.
- A thread that already carries a priority label is not re-processed on the next trigger run.
notes: Converted from TODO.md item 2. The original text said `_auto/priority/1-critical`; that prefix is stale, since LABEL_PREFIX is '' (foxhole.js:8).
